title: Retraining is a manual run on Matt's machine, with weights committed to the repo
context: docs/HOW-TO-retrain-synth.md has Matt run train_synth.py --from-vault locally and commit weights/tpms.json; the page picks it up on next load. The README calls this Pattern A and plans a GitHub Actions retrain (Pattern B). Filters such as --max-norm 1.3 and --solver-version decide which Vault rows train.

options.name: Manual local retrain, weights in git (current)
options.summary: Matt runs the trainer when the Vault drift counter says so, then commits.
pros: Full control and a human looks at every R² before it ships
cons: Retraining cannot happen in a session VM
Large binary-ish file in every retrain commit

options.name: GitHub Actions retrain opening a PR (Pattern B)
options.summary: A button runs the trainer on Actions against Vault and opens a PR with the new weights.
pros: Repeatable, logged, anyone can trigger it
Review still happens on the PR
cons: Needs Vault credentials in Actions secrets
Still commits the weights unless paired with release assets

options.name: Weights as release assets or object storage
options.summary: Keep the trainer manual or automated but publish weights outside git history.
cons: Page needs a versioned URL; rollback is less obvious

recommendation: README "Retraining" names Pattern A as today's state; docs/HOW-TO-retrain-synth.md and CLAUDE.md say retraining runs on Matt's machine.
